turns: What is the minimum attendance I need to write the end-semester exam?
results.answer:
You need at least 75% attendance in each course to be allowed to write the end-semester examination for that course. Theory and lab courses are counted separately. Attendance is counted from the first working day of the semester to the last instructional day, as recorded by the course faculty on the attendance portal.  [1]

Sources:
[1] Attendance Requirements Policy (ATT-2023-01, issued 10 Jul 2023), Section 1

turns: Can I get attendance condonation and what is the fee?
results.answer:
With effect from the odd semester of academic year 2024-25, you may apply for condonation of attendance shortage only if your attendance in the course is between 70% and 74% (earlier limit: 65%). The condonation fee is now Rs. 500 per course (earlier fee: Rs. 300). The application route (class advisor to HoD) and the need for documentary proof such as a medical certificate are unchanged. Attendance below 70% cannot be condoned.  [1]

Update: this reflects the more recent circular ATT-2024-03 (issued 5 Aug 2024), which replaces Section 3 of the earlier Attendance Requirements Policy (ATT-2023-01, issued 10 Jul 2023).

Sources:
[1] Circular - Revision of Attendance Condonation Rules (ATT-2024-03, issued 5 Aug 2024), Section 1

turns: How do I apply for re-evaluation?
results.answer:
Who can apply for re-evaluation [1]
Re-evaluation is available for theory papers only. Lab, practical and project viva results cannot be re-evaluated. You must have appeared for the exam.

Steps to request re-evaluation [2]
1. Optionally request a photocopy of your answer script using Form PC-02 to see how your paper was marked.
2. Fill in Re-evaluation Form RE-01 with your register number, course code and exam session.
3. Pay the re-evaluation fee for each paper and keep the receipt.
4. Submit Form RE-01 and the fee receipt at the Controller of Examinations office before the window closes.
5. Re-evaluation results are announced within 15 working days.

New application window and fee [3]
For results published on or after 1 February 2025, the application window for re-evaluation is 7 working days from the result publication date (earlier: 5 working days) and the fee is Rs. 1500 per paper (earlier: Rs. 1000). The photocopy fee stays at Rs. 300 per paper. Results published before 1 February 2025 continue under the earlier window and fee.

Update: this reflects the more recent circular REV-2025-02 (issued 20 Jan 2025), which replaces Section 2 of the earlier Re-evaluation and Photocopy Procedure (REV-2023-07, issued 15 Sep 2023).

Sources:
[1] Re-evaluation and Photocopy Procedure (REV-2023-07, issued 15 Sep 2023), Section 1
[2] Re-evaluation and Photocopy Procedure (REV-2023-07, issued 15 Sep 2023), Section 3
[3] Circular - Revised Re-evaluation Window and Fee (REV-2025-02, issued 20 Jan 2025), Section 1

turns: What should I do if there is a fire in the lab?
results.answer:
Fire emergency [1]
In case of fire, switch off the main power supply if it is safe to do so, raise the alarm, leave the lab through the nearest marked exit and gather at the assembly point. Use a fire extinguisher only if you have been trained and the fire is small.

Reporting incidents [2]
Report any injury, spill, fire or equipment damage to the lab in-charge immediately and fill in Incident Form LS-01 within 24 hours.

Sources:
[1] Laboratory Safety Guidelines (LAB-2023-05, issued 20 Jul 2023), Section 4
[2] Laboratory Safety Guidelines (LAB-2023-05, issued 20 Jul 2023), Section 3

turns: Can I carry my mobile phone into the exam hall if it is switched off?
results.answer:
Items not allowed in the exam hall [1]
Mobile phones, smart watches, earphones, programmable calculators and any written or printed material are not allowed, even if a phone is switched off. Leave such items at the designated counter at your own risk, or do not bring them.

Documents you must carry [2]
Carry your college ID card and your hall ticket to every exam. You will not be allowed to write without a hall ticket. If you lost it, collect a duplicate from the Controller of Examinations office (fee Rs. 200) before the exam.

Sources:
[1] Examination Instructions for Candidates (EXM-2023-04, issued 1 Sep 2023), Section 3
[2] Examination Instructions for Candidates (EXM-2023-04, issued 1 Sep 2023), Section 2

turns: I missed my exam because I was in the hospital. Can I write a make-up exam?
results.answer:
Who is eligible for a make-up examination [1]
You may apply for a make-up examination if you missed an end-semester exam because of hospitalisation (supported by a medical certificate and hospital record), the death of an immediate family member, or representing the university at a national-level event. Timetable clashes, oversleeping and travel delays are not valid reasons.

How to apply for a make-up examination [2]
Apply within 3 working days of the missed exam by submitting Form EX-07 with supporting documents to the Controller of Examinations office. The fee is Rs. 1000 per paper. The make-up exam is held within 30 days of the regular exam.

Sources:
[1] Make-up Examination Policy (EXM-2024-08, issued 15 Jan 2024), Section 1
[2] Make-up Examination Policy (EXM-2024-08, issued 15 Jan 2024), Section 2
